objective: Derive an exact finite one-old-edge repair test, prove sharp radius-six locality, and bound the spatial support of any fixed-budget repair.

atomic_claims.text: The two root edges ux and uy are individually frozen in every normalized saturated neighborhood.
A one-old-edge repair exists exactly when one of at most eight spoke/support edges admits a nontrivial star-preserving recoloring; at most 28 properness-filtered trials suffice.
The one-edit decision is determined by the colored radius-six ball, and two explicit star colorings on the same tree show radius five insufficient.
If a repair with at most k old changes exists, one exists with changed edges at line-graph distance at most 3k from uv; a further three-edge boundary suffices for validation.

assumptions: The given old coloring of H=G-v is globally star colored with palette {1,2,3,4,5,6}.
Graphs are finite, simple and subcubic; v is a leaf adjacent to u.
The exact one-edit criterion is stated for the saturated zero-edit obstruction case.
k is a nonnegative integer, and the edit budget counts old edges changed in the final coloring.
Colored balls are induced subgraphs with all inherited edge colors; boundary degrees are also equal in the sharpness example.
risks: No universal k-edit existence theorem is asserted.
A locally star colored abstract ball need not extend to a globally star colored graph.
The outward-blocking tree differs from C02 and is fully specified rather than silently revising that witness.
No mathematical enumeration, execution, or verification receipt is claimed.
The connected-support argument concerns simultaneous final changes, not necessarily a valid sequence of individual recolorings.
